script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. Friday — here is your SOXX recap. The portfolio closed zero point four five percent down on the session. A mixed day across the board, with memory names under pressure and AI infrastructure plays finding some footing.

Micron Technology fell nearly six percent on Friday despite an eighteen percent surge the prior session — profit-taking and rate concerns erasing much of Thursday's historic move in a single afternoon.

No macro data was available for Friday's session. Markets closed out the month of July with semiconductor names diverging sharply — equipment makers and networking chip names outperformed while memory and legacy compute lagged. The Nasdaq composite finished the session modestly positive, providing a partial cushion for the broader chip complex.

The dominant story Friday centered on Micron Technology, and it is worth unpacking carefully. Micron surged approximately eighteen percent Thursday following earnings — a historic single-session move driven by strong memory demand signals from cloud and device customers, including Amazon's announced two hundred twenty billion dollar artificial intelligence infrastructure commitment. Friday told a different story. Shares fell five point nine percent as profit-taking overwhelmed the bullish narrative. Analysts at several firms note that Wall Street has repeatedly underestimated Micron's earnings trajectory, yet the stock continues to face technical resistance after such a steep near-term move. The key tension heading into next week: does the demand signal from hyperscalers represent a durable cycle, or a pull-forward? That question will define how Micron trades through August.

Advanced Micro Devices was down one point nine zero percent on Friday's session. Earnings are now the central focus. Seeking Alpha moved to a Hold rating ahead of the print, citing stretched valuation after a generational run on artificial intelligence demand. At the same time, Baird issued the highest price target on Wall Street following a brutal July selloff, and a surprise Microsoft announcement may have provided the catalyst the bull case needed. Chief Executive Lisa Su, speaking publicly on July twenty-fourth, emphasized what happens when artificial intelligence infrastructure moves from build-out to active deployment — a narrative that could drive the next leg if earnings confirm it. Semiconductor exchange-traded funds, including this portfolio's benchmark, pulled in a combined nine point eight billion dollars this week on chip optimism.

Micron Technology was down five point nine zero percent on Friday's session. As covered in the top story, Thursday's eighteen percent surge gave way to Friday pullback driven by profit-taking and rate sensitivity. The two-day whipsaw captures the current market psychology around memory names precisely.

Nvidia Corporation was up two point nine three percent on Friday's session. The company's valuation has now declined to levels last seen in twenty-nineteen even as it posted a record quarter, according to reporting from Yahoo Finance. Analysts note the gap between Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices on valuation metrics has widened further. Watch the next analyst day commentary closely.

Broadcom was up zero point three seven percent on Friday's session. The name continues to benefit from strong custom artificial intelligence silicon demand from hyperscaler customers. No specific news broke Friday, but relative stability here reflects confidence in its diversified revenue base.

Intel Corporation was down one point zero two percent on Friday's session. The company remains in the middle of a multi-year restructuring, and Friday's modest decline tracks with broader pressure on legacy compute names. No fresh catalyst emerged, but the foundry timeline remains the key variable to monitor.

Applied Materials was up one point one eight percent on Friday's session. Equipment makers broadly outperformed on Friday, reflecting sustained capital expenditure commitments from chipmakers globally. Applied Materials is a direct beneficiary of any capacity expansion cycle, and the demand signals from Micron's earnings add credibility to that thesis.

KLA Corporation was up one point three eight percent on Friday's session. Like Applied Materials, KLA held well as the equipment segment demonstrated resilience. Process control spending tends to be sticky even in softer cycles, giving the name relative defensive characteristics within this portfolio.

Marvell Technology was up two point three two percent on Friday's session. Custom silicon for artificial intelligence data center applications continues to underpin the bull case, and Friday's move reflects growing investor confidence that Marvell's design win pipeline is materializing.

Lam Research Corporation was down one point five eight percent on Friday's session. The name lagged its equipment peers on Friday without a clear single catalyst. Etch and deposition tool demand remains tied to memory investment cycles, which may explain some sympathy pressure from Micron's Friday decline.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing was up zero point two three percent on Friday's session. A marginal positive close for the world's largest contract chipmaker. Advanced packaging demand, particularly for artificial intelligence accelerators, remains the near-term growth driver. Geopolitical noise around Taiwan remains a perennial risk factor to monitor.

Three items to watch over the next forty-eight hours. First, Advanced Micro Devices earnings — the print will either validate or challenge Baird's aggressive price target and the Microsoft catalyst thesis. Second, any Federal Reserve commentary from Chair Kevin Warsh, whose perceived hawkishness has weighed on rate-sensitive growth names. Third, July manufacturing data releases, which will give early reads on semiconductor equipment order trends heading into the back half of twenty twenty-six.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Advanced Micro Devices earnings will be the defining moment for this portfolio next week — watch that print closely.
